Spot - 2 years, 57lbs, English Hound Mix, Spayed 

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Their Foster Family Says: "Spot is an absolute love bug—friendly, curious, affectionate, and convinced that every human she meets is a new best friend! Her favorite thing is cuddling with her foster mom and dad after a nice long walk, though she’s also a big fan of balls, chew toys, and stuffed animals (which don’t tend to stay stuffed for long!). At home, Spot is a total shadow who happily follows her foster parents everywhere—even to the bathroom—and starts each morning by waking them up with kisses. She loves getting outside and exploring, but leash manners are definitely still a work in progress, especially when an exciting bird or squirrel catches her eye! She’ll need a patient, committed family who is willing to work consistently with her on leash skills and continue reinforcing her basic training. A semi-active home that enjoys walks, playtime, and plenty of quality time together would be a great fit for this sweet, playful girl. Above all, Spot loves being with her people and will reward their patience with endless affection, cuddles, and devotion."

Level of dog ownership experience required:
INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.)

Energy Level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs. 

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello. 

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc. 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. 

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) 
Adjusting – Might cry for a few minutes when you first leave the house but settles pretty quickly and has no problem being left alone otherwise. 

LEASH MANNERS
WTF is a leash – Pulls hard. Zig zags like crazy. Has no idea how to walk on a leash or doesn’t have outside privileges yet (too young) getting better every day!! 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO. 
Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction.

CRATE TRAINING
Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

She can not do city life. Great with other dogs - currently in a foster home with a yard and two dogs and she's living her best life! This puppy is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) POTTY TRAINING - Yes she's potty trained. Her Foster Mom Says: "Dani has been an absolute joy to take care of while she waits for her forever family. She exhibits all of the characteristics of a herding breed. She's sweet, highly intelligent, clever and independent. Although she is very high energy, she loves her breaks and naps like a typical puppy. She has an internal clock that wakes her up at the same time every day (I love that for me) and she knows when it's time for breakfast, snacks and dinner. If you're late for any of those, she will let you know with mouthy play ;) She does so well with my younger dog who is also a herding breed and she gives space to my senior dog who isn't as up to playtime (but that doesn't mean she doesn't try to rile her up from time to time). Dani loves to be outside and the sound of the leash and keys ignites so much excitement from her! Her walks get better by the day as she came terrified of loud sounds but is learning to adapt. She still gets spooked and might want to hightail it back to the house, but with a few calming pep talks and some treat motivation, she gets right back on track. She also loves to play wrestle and chase outside and tends to dig for treasures aka sticks! Her own designated dig box would be ideal!"

Level of dog ownership experience required:
INTERMEDIATE – As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. Relevant puppy care experience is a huge plus, but bare minimum the adopter must have TONS of time and patience. Raising a puppy can be a lot of fun, but it’s also  tremendous work. Puppies’ personalities and exercise/stimulation requirements change dramatically between now and when they’re a year old as their bodies and brains develop, so an active lifestyle and the ability to adapt to a pup’s evolving needs are a must. We strongly urge professional dog training with a rewards based trainer from the get go. Adults only or kids ages 8 and up – all puppies go through a mouthy, rambunctious phase and often accidentally hurt children when playing. PLEASE DO YOUR OWN BREED RESEARCH to make sure you have a better understanding of the kind of temperament and exercise requirements this dog may have as an adult.

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

POTTY TRAINING - Yes she's potty trained.  She's fully potty trained.

TOLERANCE TO CITY - Can't do the city. Needs a home in the burbs :) 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS - She's shy at first with strangers but warms up to them quick. I have not witnessed any aggression or fear.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN - Okay in a home with older kids. Too playful to be in a home with younger kids. 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS - She is playful and social with dogs in the home/yard setting. When she sees dogs, she wants to play with them. She doesn't seem phased by the size of the dog.

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS - She chases and barks at squirrels. She hasn't had close up interaction/play with cats but she barks at them when she sees them in the neighbor's yard. 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR - Very mouthy - wants to play with her mouth. Learning she can't do this with humans. But respectufl of belongings. 

SEPARATION ANXIETY - Will cry when you first leave her home alone. But then settles down. 

LEASH MANNERS - She is great with the leash. Only pulls if she gets spooked but for the most part, she's fine.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL - She is lower level! She comes to you and lays next to you but gets up for her own space pretty quickly. 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO - She is definitely a jumper and needs more training. She listens to commands to get down unless she's really excited. 

CRATE TRAINING - She goes in and out whenever she wants. She lays in it for her alone time and to eat. If I need her to go in, she won't just go in it because she seems to know that means I have to leave lol. So I put a treat inside and she goes in.
She does try to eat the food and treats of the other dogs, so I give her her food in the crate. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP and Bordetella vaccines, spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. (For dogs under 4 months old, adopters will need to finish the DHPP vaccine series and administer the Rabies vaccine at 16 weeks of age.)

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives.

She does try to eat the food and treats of the other dogs, so I give her her food in the crate.

Yes – Few or no accidents

Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range. She will pee on clothing left on the floor and the bath mat.

High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time, loves to lay around in bed, and is happy to be held.

pets.description: Teddy - 6 months & 20lbs (as of 09/10), Terrier/Shepherd Mix, Neutered We're not sure of this guys breed mix, he's a smaller guy with big do features, a stunner! If you want to see a video of this dog please click here . Expected to be about 35lbs full grown This puppy is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Their Foster Family Says: " Teddy is SO curious! Listens to the wind. Wants to say hi to other dogs (all sizes) and approaches with energy and playful vibes but then retreats in self consciousness and hides behind my legs. He wants to pick up every stick and leaf and parade them around as his new treasures but drops them easily and moves on to the next street-delight. Teddy has learned “sit” and sometimes gets “paw”! He is treat motivated and highly focused on his bones/chew treats for hours. He also LOVES his human (immediately started to treat me like a mama). He wants to unravel his bones while sitting next to me and when I’m standing up and walking about he will follow me around squeaking and chewing his toy. His noises are soooo sweet. Squeaks and whimpers to express delight and rarely barks — only when someone in the hall of my apartment building startles him. He got something sticky stuck to his tail and I was worried that pulling it off he would be upset but no! He was a patient patient; displaying bravery/kindness even as his tail was jostled and pulled. He's a boy with a sweet and gentle soul and would do best with people who are patient as he continues to figure out how to be brave and make friends." Level of dog ownership experience required: INTERMEDIATE – As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.) Relevant puppy care experience is a huge plus, but bare minimum the adopter must have TONS of time and patience. Raising a puppy can be a lot of fun, but it’s also tremendous work. Puppies’ personalities and exercise/stimulation requirements change dramatically between now and when they’re a year old as their bodies and brains develop, so an active lifestyle and the ability to adapt to a pup’s evolving needs are a must. We strongly urge professional dog training with a rewards based trainer from the get go. Adults only or kids ages 8 and up – all puppies go through a mouthy, rambunctious phase and often accidentally hurt children when playing. PLEASE DO YOUR OWN BREED RESEARCH to make sure you have a better understanding of the kind of temperament and exercise requirements this dog may have as an adult. Energy Level: MEDIUM – Very young puppies sleep and nap a lot, but their energy level skyrockets when they become teens (4 months to around a year). As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 60 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day at a minimum. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) TOLERANCE TO CITY Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs. Teddy is easily spooked by loud cars/trucks/sirens. He can be a little skittish at a passing skateboarder. Ideal home would be somewhere calm Although, I think he needs more time to get acclimated. POTTY TRAINING Yes – Few or no accidents. He still relies on wee pads for peeing, as he drinks quite a bit of water. He has learned to go number 2 outside. COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. Teddy is very timid around strangers. He recoils if a stranger tries to approach him. If a stranger comes to my home, he will bark, but will not approach the person. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision) Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) He has moments when he can be mouthy and gets the zoomies. He can be skittish among young children. SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS Still working on it – Either retreats from other dogs or barks at them/leash reactive. Needs more socialization training or may just be a dog that prefers human company. He is very afraid of dogs larger than him. He shows some interest in smaller dogs, but needs to be trained to approach them calmly. MOUTHY BEHAVIOR Needs training – Is either still in the puppy stage or was never trained. Tries to put their mouth on your hands when playing or needs attention, grabs leash, chews on your personal belongings. Teddy has a propensity to bite hands. I've noticed this occurs after he's energized from a walk. Firm correction usually stops him. He also likes to bite the leash on walks. If left unsupervised, he will try to eat shoes, grabs clothes within reach, eat cardboard, dig in bathroom trashcan. SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) Adjusting – Might cry for a few minutes when you first leave the house but settles pretty quickly and has no problem being left alone otherwise. I've left him alone for a couple of hours in some cases, and he does whimper, but the eventually settles down with his chew toys. He's always placed in the crate when I leave him alone, so there's no destruction. As he's a puppy, I cannot trust him to roam around my apt alone. LEASH MANNERS Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. He's still getting the hang of walking on one's side. He tends to zigzag left to right during walks. He sometimes gets eager and starts pulling ahead. He will walk and then stop walking, if he's walking ahead, which he tends to do. He also has gotten comfortable sniffing. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL Medium – Likes to snuggle when he's in the mood but often stays in his own bed. I would say medium to high. He likes to be on the sofa next to me and loves to be held when we're sitting at the park. I don't allow him to sleep on my bed. He sleeps throughout the night in his crate. JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction. CRATE TRAINING Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night. He has adjusted quite well to the crate. He goes in easily, with some mild coaxing at times. He sleeps through the night in the crate with no whining. I will leave him in the crate whenever I step out. Medical status: Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP and Bordetella vaccines, spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. (For dogs under 4 months old, adopters will need to finish the DHPP vaccine series and administer the Rabies vaccine at 16 weeks of age.) How did this dog end up with Social Tees? Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses. This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes. LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc

Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. He's still getting the hang of walking on one's side. He tends to zigzag left to right during walks. Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction.

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Level of dog ownership experience required:
BEGINNER – “Beginner” doesn’t necessarily mean easy as all dogs will require time, work, and patience, but we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale because of their breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup.

Energy Level:
LOWER – Pretty chill indoors and won’t demand endless amounts of stimulation and exercise but still needs a few walks a day (20-30 min each) for potty breaks and to stretch their legs.

Okay in the city?
We don’t know yet because this pup is brand new to us. Most adult dogs do well in the city after they’ve had time to adjust to a new environment, but some never adapt and need homes in the burbs. 

Potty trained?
Probably! Adults usually are, but all will have transitional accidents for the first week or so. A consistent walking route and schedule plus finding spots with grass or dirt can help.

Social with other dogs?
Yes, but we don’t know to what degree yet. Some like to wrestle with every passing pup, others can coexist well but prefer to keep to themselves. We’ll learn more soon.

Social with cats?
Not sure yet! Some breed mixes that are generally NOT great matches for homes with cats include large hounds, huskies, and shepherds. 

Comfortable with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)
We’re not sure yet, but we try to err on the side of caution. Respectful kids ages 8 and up are probably a safe bet. Children must always be monitored and taught to interact with dogs of any age carefully. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc

Outdoors, she's quick to use the bathroom but is still getting her city legs and can be a bit stop and go if she gets spooked by people or noises. TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to city- she's getting better every day but still gets nervous or freezes with loud noise or crowds. Usually needs to be toted to the nearby park and then walks okay once there (but she's getting better about being able to walk home on her own!)

POTTY TRAINING
Yes- few accidents first few days but to be expected!

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
In between bean

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN
Maybe for age 12 and up- skittish with loud noise and sudden movement, but once she is comfortable with you, she is pretty energetic and jumpy which wouldn't be great for small kids

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes- caveat that she is generally not very interested because of being on the skittish side

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS
Yes- she hasn't interacted with other animals but does not show interest in birds on the street

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Working on it- nibbles on hands (responds to correction), and will chew things she is not supposed to if you leave them out. definitely requires puppy proofing of the home! no furniture or anything major, just clothes or the occasional shoe

SEPARATION ANXIETY
Adjusting- may cry or pace a little but generally fine being home alone for hours at a time

LEASH MANNERS
WTF is a leash- 100% has never been on a leash before, the first time she went out she was SO confused by it lol. She's getting better but we're focusing on being able to walk generally before improving her leash manners :)

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
Medium/High- will generally be right next to you if she's napping and sleeps on my pillow right next to me at night 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Depends on the person- with strangers it's very calm but with me she is very excited and jumpy. Listens well to correction.

CRATE TRAINING
Not at all- puppy proofed the home and she free roams when alone

pets.name: Lil Bit
pets.description: Lil Bit - 8 years, 11lbs, Chiweenie, Neutered - Our vet estimates him to be anywhere between 5 to 7 and possibly even 8. Please click here to see videos of little bit. His Foster Family Says: "Lil Bit has been the sweetest foster dog we could have asked for. From the moment we picked him up, he has been incredibly sweet, calm, trusting, and well behaved. He gets along wonderfully with our dogs and has such a kind, gentle soul. At home, Lil Bit is calm and affectionate. He loves snuggling with us on the couch and being near his people, but in a gentle, independent way that is never overly needy. Lil Bit - 8 years, 11lbs, Chiweenie, Neutered - Our vet estimates him to be anywhere between 5 to 7 and possibly even 8. 

Please click here to see videos of little bit. 

His Foster Family Says: "Lil Bit has been the sweetest foster dog we could have asked for. From the moment we picked him up, he has been incredibly sweet, calm, trusting, and well behaved. He gets along wonderfully with our dogs and has such a kind, gentle soul. At home, Lil Bit is calm and affectionate. He loves snuggling with us on the couch and being near his people, but in a gentle, independent way that is never overly needy. He is very quiet and is happy relaxing, sleeping, or watching the world go by from our window sill, one of his favorite spots. His sweet little face and adorable snaggle tooth are just as charming as his affectionate personality! Lil Bit is also incredibly easy to care for. He is fully house trained and enjoys one longer walk each day along with a couple of shorter walks. He is not reactive on walks. He approaches the world with a wonderful sense of curiously and trust, and really enjoys meeting other dogs and people he passes on walks."

Level of dog ownership experience needed:
FLEXIBLE – We predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale with regard to exercise and mental stimulation requirements, but seniors tend to need a lot of help and understanding when it comes to lifestyle and veterinary issues. Seniors usually need quiet, calm environments and routines and do not do well with a lot of bustle, change, and rambunctious movement (kids and young playful dogs, for instance). This dog’s adopter will need to be prepared for senior health challenges, which means frequent vet visits and very expensive veterinary bills. (An annual senior blood panel alone costs around $500 in NYC.) Senior care can also take an emotional toll on their humans. Adopting a mature pup is a wonderful thing to do, but it can also be difficult. 

Energy level:
LOWER – Pretty chill indoors and won’t demand endless amounts of stimulation and exercise but still needs a few short walks a day (10-30 min each) for potty breaks and to stretch their legs

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). He is sometimes startled by random loud noises but has been able to get around the city, even louder parts, fine. We do live in a more calm part of Brooklyn but he did go on the Subway for the first time yesterday and was totally fine and not scared at all. 

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello. 

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Yes for most ages – very confident, gentle, low energy, tolerant, not mouthy 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Yes – Seems to get along with cats etc., either tries to play with them or is mostly uninterested

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime

SEPARATION ANXIETY
Adjusting – Might cry for a few minutes when you first leave the house but settles pretty quickly and has no problem being left alone otherwise. 

LEASH MANNERS
Old Pro – Doesn’t pull hard or need much direction. 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
Medium – Likes to snuggle when he's in the mood but often stays in his own bed 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor. 

CRATE TRAINING
Don't use it -  We only tried crating him once and he was whimpering a lot so we let him out. We didn't find the need to keep him in there because he has been very well behaved.

Medical status:
Healthy for their age as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. Adopters will need to be ready for senior care – at a minimum, that will be annual checkups including senior bloodwork and a dental post adoption (most senior rescues need one).

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Thier Foster Family Says: "Elroy is truly one of the happiest and most lovable pups ever. I would definitely consider him a “Velcro dog.” He loves being around his people and will follow you around the house, checking in throughout the day for some love and attention. Every time you walk past him, he will expect to be pet, preferably with his belly up! He absolutely LOVES people. If he could have a “Please Pet Me” sign attached to him, he would. He is the definition of a social butterfly and loves meeting new people and dogs.Elroy especially enjoys meeting smaller dogs, but he does well with dogs of all sizes. He can just be a little more cautious when meeting bigger dogs at first. He also does not seem to realize that he is a big dog! He will happily try to sit on your lap or put his paws on you when he gets excited or wants attention. Elroy is an incredibly calm pup overall. He loves taking naps in the funniest positions and can pretty much fall asleep anywhere. Elroy does very well in social settings. He is comfortable sitting beside you at a restaurant, hanging out in coffee shops, going into stores, and playing at dog parks. He does great on city walks and has been adjusting really well to his surroundings. Elroy is very food-motivated and eager to learn. He has already learned commands such as sit, lay down, paw, and come, and he is very responsive to correction. One of his funniest habits is that he loves stealing socks and carrying them around like they are his emotional support items. He is also getting the hang of playing with toys. He is not particularly interested in squeaky toys, but he absolutely ADORES balls of all kinds, including tennis balls, rubber balls, baseballs, etc. Sometimes he will even carry a tennis ball around in his mouth just for fun and entertain himself by playing with it. Elroy is a major cuddle bug. Any opportunity you give him to cuddle, he will happily take it. pets.name: Ocean
pets.description: Ocean - 5 months & 20lbs (as of 9/4), Chi/Terrier Mix, Spayed Expected to be about 30lbs full grown This puppy is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Thier Foster Parent Says: " Ocean has made a lot of progress since coming into our home. She's doing much better with walking outside and is getting the hang of potty training. She isn’t 100% yet but she’s getting there. She needs to go out about 4-5 times. She still needs time to warm up to new people and places but has gotten so much more comfortable. Her silly and playful personality is starting to come out. She’s still a puppy so she likes to chew things up like shoes and books but can be redirected to play with toys or chew on a treat. She's responsive to correction. She is no longer hiding when she has to poo which is good and she’s like clockwork if you take her out after meals. She is not as territorial with food. She knows she will be getting fed.She loves the kids and our dog. She prefers to be next to somebody. She needs stimulation and play time. I think it helps her feel relaxed and happy. She still instinctually moves when we reach toward her to pet her but she doesn’t run away. She’s starting to trust more, which is super rewarding to experience. She will stop when she hears noises like cars and other dogs but she doesn’t freeze or shrink back like she used to. We crate her when we leave for short periods but leave her out of the crate when we are out for longer. Last night we tried leaving her out of the crate and she did fine. No accidents or restlessness. Ocean is going to be a wonderful dog, she just needs a someone who will show her love and kindness and patience." Level of dog ownership experience required: INTERMEDIATE – As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.) Relevant puppy care experience is a huge plus, but bare minimum the adopter must have TONS of time and patience. Raising a puppy can be a lot of fun, but it’s also tremendous work. Puppies’ personalities and exercise/stimulation requirements change dramatically between now and when they’re a year old as their bodies and brains develop, so an active lifestyle and the ability to adapt to a pup’s evolving needs are a must. We strongly urge professional dog training with a rewards based trainer from the get go. Adults only or kids ages 8 and up – all puppies go through a mouthy, rambunctious phase and often accidentally hurt children when playing. PLEASE DO YOUR OWN BREED RESEARCH to make sure you have a better understanding of the kind of temperament and exercise requirements this dog may have as an adult. Energy level: MEDIUM – Very young puppies sleep and nap a lot, but their energy level skyrockets when they become teens (4 months to around a year). As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 60 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day at a minimum. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) TOLERANCE TO CITY Adjusting to the city – would love a home in a calm area POTTY TRAINING Working on this skill. Puppies under 12 weeks old are often on track with their wee pad skills, but they’re too young to walk outside in public NYC areas yet because they haven’t finished their puppy vaccine series. Puppies older than 12 weeks are usually learning to do their business outside. Potty training takes a lot of patience, consistency, and clean up. COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision) Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.) Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc. MOUTHY BEHAVIOR Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) Ocean is doing great being left home alone now. Most puppies have some level of separation anxiety as they learn to self soothe. Often they cry the first 10+ minutes at night or when they are left home alone or in a crate. Consistent training and alone time is crucial. LEASH MANNERS Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL Medium – Likes to snuggle when he's in the mood but often stays in his own bed JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction. CRATE TRAINING Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night. Expected to be about 30lbs full grown

Thier Foster Parent Says: "Ocean has made a lot of progress since coming into our home. She's doing much better with walking outside and is getting the hang of potty training. She isn’t 100% yet but she’s getting there. She needs to go out about 4-5 times.
She still needs time to warm up to new people and places but has gotten so much more comfortable. Her silly and playful personality is starting to come out.  She’s still a puppy so she likes to chew things up like shoes and books but can be redirected to play with toys or chew on a treat. She's responsive to correction. She is no longer hiding when she has to poo which is good and she’s like clockwork if you take her out after meals. She is not as territorial with food. She knows she will be getting fed.She loves the kids and our dog. She prefers to be next to somebody. She needs stimulation and play time. I think it helps her feel relaxed and happy. She still instinctually moves when we reach toward her to pet her but she doesn’t run away. She’s starting to trust more, which is super rewarding to experience. She will stop when she hears noises like cars and other dogs but she doesn’t freeze or shrink back like she used to. We crate her when we leave for short periods but leave her out of the crate when we are out for longer. Last night we tried leaving her out of the crate and she did fine. No accidents or restlessness. Ocean is going to be a wonderful dog, she just needs a someone who will show her love and kindness and patience." 

Level of dog ownership experience required:
INTERMEDIATE – As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.) Relevant puppy care experience is a huge plus, but bare minimum the adopter must have TONS of time and patience. Raising a puppy can be a lot of fun, but it’s also  tremendous work. Puppies’ personalities and exercise/stimulation requirements change dramatically between now and when they’re a year old as their bodies and brains develop, so an active lifestyle and the ability to adapt to a pup’s evolving needs are a must. We strongly urge professional dog training with a rewards based trainer from the get go. Adults only or kids ages 8 and up – all puppies go through a mouthy, rambunctious phase and often accidentally hurt children when playing. PLEASE DO YOUR OWN BREED RESEARCH to make sure you have a better understanding of the kind of temperament and exercise requirements this dog may have as an adult.

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Very young puppies sleep and nap a lot, but their energy level skyrockets when they become teens (4 months to around a year). As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 60 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day at a minimum. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – would love a home in a calm area 

POTTY TRAINING
Working on this skill. Puppies under 12 weeks old are often on track with their wee pad skills, but they’re too young to walk outside in public NYC areas yet because they haven’t finished their puppy vaccine series. Puppies older than 12 weeks are usually learning to do their business outside. Potty training takes a lot of patience, consistency, and clean up. 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. 

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) 

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc. 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. 

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) 
Ocean is doing great being left home alone now. Most puppies have some level of separation anxiety as they learn to self soothe. Often they cry the first 10+ minutes at night or when they are left home alone or in a crate. Consistent training and alone time is crucial.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
Medium – Likes to snuggle when he's in the mood but often stays in his own bed 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction.

CRATE TRAINING
Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP and Bordetella vaccines, spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. (For dogs under 4 months old, adopters will need to finish the DHPP vaccine series and administer the Rabies vaccine at 16 weeks of age.)

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses. 

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

Sorrel - 3 years, 9lbs, Chiweenie, Spayed 

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Our Team Says: "Sorrel would do best in a calm area. She's still working on her confidence outdoors. She wouldn't say no to a home in the burbs or beyond." 

Thier Foster Parent Says: "Sorrel is literally a tiny baby Living in a big, very scary world. At a whopping 9 pounds, she has decided that the safest place to be is… directly on your skin. If you’re sitting down, congratulations!!! you now have a chiweenie dog attached to you. She LOVESSSSS salmon skin treats. Like, LOVES THEM. She will absolutely bark at you for more because apparently 47 treats is never enough.  She’s also learning how to sit, which is a BIG deal because, as everyone knows, chiweenie dogs have approximately zero interest in taking orders. She’s doing great and slowly realizing that listening = snacks.  Outside, Sorrel is still a scaredy baby. Going out to potty is a whole production because literally EVERYTHING is terrifying. A leaf? Scary. A noise? SCARY. A person existing nearby? CALL 911. She’s only 9 pounds, so the world is understandably HUGE to her. With patience, reassurance, and someone willing to let her take things at her own pace, she’s learning that outside isn’t so scary after all. Sorrel is crate trained and has discovered that her bed is her little safe space. When she wants peace and quiet, she knows exactly where to go. She isn’t super toy motivated yet and would much rather play with you than a squeaky toy, but who knows, maybe her inner toy gremlin is still loading. She currently has two foster sisters: one around her tiny size and one big potato. She absolutely loves snuggling with them when she’s in the mood, but Sorrel is also very good at communicating when she’s had enough. She’ll happily cuddle… until she doesn't, and then she will politely let you know that your services are no longer required. 
Sorrel is looking for someone who understands that she’s still a baby, who will give her time to build confidence, and who doesn’t mind having a 9 pound personal shadow following them around." 

Level of dog ownership experience required:
BEGINNER – “Beginner” doesn’t necessarily mean easy as all dogs will require time, work, and patience, but we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale because of their breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. 

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs. 

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Good with other dogs – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example). Currently living with two dogs :) 

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Yes – Seems to get along with cats etc., either tries to play with them or is mostly uninterested 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) 
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house. 
LEASH MANNERS

Old Pro – Doesn’t pull hard or need much direction. 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

**MOUTHY BEHAVIOR**  

Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime

Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.

**Old Pro** – Doesn’t pull hard or need much direction.   

  

**CUDDLE BUG LEVEL**  

**High** – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time

**Calm Greetings** – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor.

**How did this dog end up with Social Tees?**  

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

pets.description: Romeo - 10 years & 10lbs, Mini Aussie, Neutered Please click here to learn more about Romeo! This senior angel is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Our Team Says: "Romeo is a very special senior boy. This poor guys spent his whole life living with a breeder. So he's just now learning how to be a real dog. He needs a home outside of the city ideally and with another dog. He must go to a home with another dog, he finds a lot of comfort in having a dog friend. His adopters need to be patient people as he will take a while to get used to his new home and people. He's come a long way. And we're very proud of him." His Foster Mom Says: " Romeo is a lover but plays hard to get. He is lovely natured but a timid dog who was terrified at first. He's come leaps and bounds but is still hesitant of crowds and loud noises. Gaining Romeo's trust and seeing him come out of his shell has been the most rewarding experience. He hasn't recognized "Romeo" but "Splodge" works and with his beautiful blue eyes, adorable floppy ears, enthusiastic waggly snub tail, and snaggle toothed smile, his gorgeous soft coat is well ... splodgy. Some of the most adorable things about Romeo are that he's smart, polite, easy-going and willing to learn. A true gentleman. He loves a tummy scratch and gets all prepared for it. On waking up in the morning, he is the most playfull - he adorably scrubs his face and ears with his long paws. He's a leggy boy and is very agile (he has the longest stretches). Although most of the time, he is happy to just rest and be near you. After some tummy upsets, he's been doing really well on an easy to digest diet (Hills Science Biome). We can't wait to see him find his forever home." Level of dog ownership experience needed: FLEXIBLE – We predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale with regard to exercise and mental stimulation requirements, but seniors tend to need a lot of help and understanding when it comes to lifestyle and veterinary issues. Seniors usually need quiet, calm environments and routines and do not do well with a lot of bustle, change, and rambunctious movement (kids and young playful dogs, for instance). This dog’s adopter will need to be prepared for senior health challenges, which means frequent vet visits and very expensive veterinary bills. (An annual senior blood panel alone costs around $500 in NYC.) Senior care can also take an emotional toll on their humans. Adopting a mature pup is a wonderful thing to do, but it can also be difficult. Energy Level: LOWER – Pretty chill indoors and won’t demand endless amounts of stimulation and exercise but still needs a few short walks a day (10-30 min each) for potty breaks and to stretch their legs Tolerance to City : Adjusting to the City. Romeo is scared of crowds and sharp/loud noises, would do best out of the city. Potty Trained: Yes. Comfort Level with Strangers: Wallflower, takeas a long time to warm up to new people. Behavior with Children: Not a match with a home with kids. He's very gently but easily spooked. Older respectful children are okay but no young children. Social Behavior with other Dogs: Still working on it, especially bigger dogs. Romeo needs space to greet dogs but he was really great with my small dog that gave him lots of space. Mouthy Behavior : Is over it. He only has 5 teeth! Respectful Behavior with Other Animals : Okay to live with a cat. Separation Anxiety: Does okay home alone Leash Manners: Getting the hang of it. When stressed, Romeo will pull on his lead and try to get away from the situation, especially within crowds. Cuddle Bug Levels: Medium. Romeo likes to stay close to but not ON you. He loves belly rubs and makes it clear when he's ready for them (he has a routine). He's ok being picked up. Jumping on People to Say Hello : Calm - doesn't do this Crate Training : Not at all in his foster home, however, Romeo likes a 'safe' space which has been various dog beds. O, and he sleeps on the human's bed at the base. Medical status: Healthy for their age as far as we know. His adopters need to be patient people as he will take a while to get used to his new home and people. He's come a long way. And we're very proud of him." 

His Foster Mom Says: "Romeo is a lover but plays hard to get. He is lovely natured but a timid dog who was terrified at first. He's come leaps and bounds but is still hesitant of crowds and loud noises. Gaining Romeo's trust and seeing him come out of his shell has been the most rewarding experience. He hasn't recognized "Romeo" but "Splodge" works and with his beautiful blue eyes, adorable floppy ears, enthusiastic waggly snub tail, and snaggle toothed smile, his gorgeous soft coat is well ... splodgy. Some of the most adorable things about Romeo are that he's smart, polite, easy-going and willing to learn. A true gentleman. He loves a tummy scratch and gets all prepared for it. On waking up in the morning, he is the most playfull - he adorably scrubs his face and ears with his long paws. He's a leggy boy and is very agile (he has the longest stretches). Although most of the time, he is happy to just rest and be near you. After some tummy upsets, he's been doing really well on an easy to digest diet (Hills Science Biome). We can't wait to see him find his forever home."

Level of dog ownership experience needed:
FLEXIBLE – We predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale with regard to exercise and mental stimulation requirements, but seniors tend to need a lot of help and understanding when it comes to lifestyle and veterinary issues. Seniors usually need quiet, calm environments and routines and do not do well with a lot of bustle, change, and rambunctious movement (kids and young playful dogs, for instance). This dog’s adopter will need to be prepared for senior health challenges, which means frequent vet visits and very expensive veterinary bills. (An annual senior blood panel alone costs around $500 in NYC.) Senior care can also take an emotional toll on their humans. Adopting a mature pup is a wonderful thing to do, but it can also be difficult. 

Energy Level:
LOWER – Pretty chill indoors and won’t demand endless amounts of stimulation and exercise but still needs a few short walks a day (10-30 min each) for potty breaks and to stretch their legs

Tolerance to City:
Adjusting to the City. Romeo is scared of crowds and sharp/loud noises, would do best out of the city. 

Potty Trained:
Yes.

Comfort Level with Strangers:
Wallflower, takeas a long time to warm up to new people. 

Behavior with Children:
Not a match with a home with kids. He's very gently but easily spooked. Older respectful children are okay but no young children. 

Social Behavior with other Dogs:
Still working on it, especially bigger dogs. Romeo needs space to greet dogs but he was really great with my small dog that gave him lots of space.

Mouthy Behavior:
Is over it.  He only has 5 teeth!

Respectful Behavior with Other Animals:
Okay to live with a cat. 

Separation Anxiety:
Does okay home alone 

Leash Manners:
Getting the hang of it. When stressed, Romeo will pull on his lead and try to get away from the situation, especially within crowds.

Cuddle Bug Levels:
Medium. Romeo likes to stay close to but not ON you. He loves belly rubs and makes it clear when he's ready for them (he has a routine). He's ok being picked up.

Jumping on People to Say Hello:
Calm - doesn't do this 

Crate Training:
Not at all in his foster home, however, Romeo likes a 'safe' space which has been various dog beds. O, and he sleeps on the human's bed at the base.

Medical status:
Healthy for their age as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. Adopters will need to be ready for senior care – at a minimum, that will be annual checkups including senior bloodwork and a dental post adoption (most senior rescues need one).

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

Energy level:
EXPERT – Very young puppies sleep and nap a lot, but their energy level skyrockets when they become teens (4 months to around a year). As an adult, this dog will need loads of structure and daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 2+ consecutive hours of quick paced movement plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

Potty trained?
Working on this skill. Puppies under 12 weeks old are often on track with their wee pad skills, but they’re too young to walk outside in public NYC areas yet because they haven’t finished their puppy vaccine series. Puppies older than 12 weeks are usually learning to do their business outside. Potty training takes a lot of patience, consistency, and clean up. 

Social with dogs?
Yes. Some puppies are shy, others are bold, but all have the potential to be taught healthy socializing skills. It’s a huge part of raising a puppy and must be done carefully. How they interact with other dogs depends largely on how their humans help them learn to. 

Social with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)
Sort of – some puppies enjoy interacting with children, others get easily overwhelmed by their energy and attention. Regardless, most puppies are not a great match for a home with kids under age 8 because they go through intense mouthy play and rambunctious phases and often accidentally hurt young kids while playing. Children must always be monitored and taught to interact with dogs of any age respectfully.  

Social with cats?
Yes. Most puppies have the potential to be friends with a cat. It’s on the adopter to know their cat’s temperament and preferences and to teach their puppy respectful manners. 

Mouthy play: 
High! All puppies go through phases where they chew your stuff and grab your hands, arms, feet… puppies naturally explore the world, play, and test boundaries with their mouths. (It also happens when they’re teething.) Their teeth are super sharp, so it can be a very painful phase for humans and other animals in the home. Proper training, outlets, and socialization are key.

Separation anxiety:
Most puppies have some level of separation anxiety as they learn to self soothe. Often they cry the first 10+ minutes at night or when they are left home alone or in a crate. Consistent training and alone time is crucial.

Leash manners:
None or learning, depending on the puppy’s age. Will need to work on this skill.  

Crate trained?
Probably not. None of our new puppies have been formally trained, but many of our foster parents/adopters choose to crate train so some of the puppies that have been with us for a little while are learning this skill. It can be a great way to keep puppies safe and teach them independence.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP and Bordetella vaccines, spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. (For dogs under 4 months old, adopters will need to finish the DHPP vaccine series and administer the Rabies vaccine at 16 weeks of age.)

pets.name: Jack
pets.description: Jack - 8 months & 35lbs, Lab Mix, Neutered Our Team Says: Jack is a sensitive dog and needs a home outside of the city. He can not be adopted out to a home in the city. Thier Foster Parent Says: " Jack is a wallflower with a heart of kindness—a gentle soul with the most irresistible puppy dog eyes you've ever seen. This sweet boy may take a little time to warm up, but once he does, you'll have the most devoted companion by your side. Jack is a classic "slow to trust, loyal forever" kind of pup. He's still learning that the world is a safe and wonderful place, and he's looking for a patient family to show him the ropes. The good news? He's incredibly treat-motivated, which makes training a breeze and bonding even easier. Once Jack feels comfortable, his true personality shines through. He loves nothing more than curling up right next to you for cozy snuggles. He's also discovered the joy of playing in the snow—watching him romp around outside is pure happiness! While he sometimes needs a little encouragement to head out the door, he's always glad he did once he's exploring the great outdoors. Jack has a wonderful temperament and gets along beautifully with his foster siblings—Addy the dog and Socks the cat—so he'd do well in a home with other gentle pets who can help him come out of his shell. If you're looking for a sweet, snuggly pup who will blossom with a little love and patience, Jack is waiting to steal your heart" ENERGY LEVEL High – Needs a daily 2-hour (or longer) window of quick paced exercise each morning in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). May also need another 40+ minute walk in the afternoon as well as significant opportunities to socialize outside the home and engage in mental stimulation activities at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re under-stimulated.) TOLERANCE TO CITY Country mouse – Needs a home outside of the city, suburbs or beyond. Terrified of walks, barely wants to move and shakes a lot, eager to get back home (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). POTTY TRAINING Yes – Few or no accidents COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS Wallflowe r – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision) Yes for most ages – very confident, gentle, low energy, tolerant, not mouthy SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.) Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc. MOUTHY BEHAVIOR Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. SEPARATION ANXIETY Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house. As long as you aren’t home while in the crate he won’t cry or bark. LEASH MANNERS Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor. Usually likes to hide. CRATE TRAINING Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night. Medical status: Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake How did this dog end up with Social Tees? Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. Jack - 8 months & 35lbs, Lab Mix, Neutered 

Our Team Says: Jack is a sensitive dog and needs a home outside of the city. He can not be adopted out to a home in the city. 

Thier Foster Parent Says: "Jack is a wallflower with a heart of kindness—a gentle soul with the most irresistible puppy dog eyes you've ever seen. This sweet boy may take a little time to warm up, but once he does, you'll have the most devoted companion by your side. Jack is a classic "slow to trust, loyal forever" kind of pup. He's still learning that the world is a safe and wonderful place, and he's looking for a patient family to show him the ropes. The good news? He's incredibly treat-motivated, which makes training a breeze and bonding even easier. Once Jack feels comfortable, his true personality shines through. He loves nothing more than curling up right next to you for cozy snuggles. He's also discovered the joy of playing in the snow—watching him romp around outside is pure happiness! While he sometimes needs a little encouragement to head out the door, he's always glad he did once he's exploring the great outdoors. Jack has a wonderful temperament and gets along beautifully with his foster siblings—Addy the dog and Socks the cat—so he'd do well in a home with other gentle pets who can help him come out of his shell. If you're looking for a sweet, snuggly pup who will blossom with a little love and patience, Jack is waiting to steal your heart"

ENERGY LEVEL
High – Needs a daily 2-hour (or longer) window of quick paced exercise each morning in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). May also need another 40+ minute walk in the afternoon as well as significant opportunities to socialize outside the home and engage in mental stimulation activities at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re under-stimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Country mouse – Needs a home outside of the city, suburbs or beyond. Terrified of walks, barely wants to move and shakes a lot, eager to get back home (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). 

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. 

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Yes for most ages – very confident, gentle, low energy, tolerant, not mouthy 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) 

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc. 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR

Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. 

SEPARATION ANXIETY
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house. As long as you aren’t home while in the crate he won’t cry or bark. 

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor. Usually likes to hide. 

CRATE TRAINING
Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

Nope – Chases and barks at cats etc., definitely not a good match for a home with cats or pocket pets

Medium – Likes to snuggle when she's in the mood but often stays in his own bed 

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO

Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.

Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Level of dog ownership experience required: INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. (ALWAYS requires adult supervision) We’re not sure yet, but we try to err on the side of caution. Respectful kids ages 8 and up are probably a safe bet. Level of dog ownership experience required:
INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.)

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

Okay in the city?
We don’t know yet because this pup is brand new to us. Most adult dogs do well in the city after they’ve had time to adjust to a new environment, but some never adapt and need homes in the burbs. 

Potty trained?
Probably! Adults usually are, but all will have transitional accidents for the first week or so. A consistent walking route and schedule plus finding spots with grass or dirt can help.

Social with other dogs?
Yes, but we don’t know to what degree yet. Some like to wrestle with every passing pup, others can coexist well but prefer to keep to themselves. We’ll learn more soon.

Social with cats?
Not sure yet! Some breed mixes that are generally NOT great matches for homes with cats include large hounds, huskies, and shepherds. 

Comfortable with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)
We’re not sure yet, but we try to err on the side of caution. Respectful kids ages 8 and up are probably a safe bet. Children must always be monitored and taught to interact with dogs of any age carefully. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake
